catalysts.headline: Oracle's 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, held virtually at 9:00am CT (record date 2026-09-21); ballot includes election of 13 directors, an advisory say-on-pay vote, ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as auditor, and a stockholder proposal on preserving shareholder-proposal access rights (board recommends voting for all management items and against the stockholder proposal)
catalysts.impact: Routine annual-meeting governance event; no standalone operational catalyst expected, though say-on-pay and director votes are data points on governance sentiment

catalysts.headline: Oracle's 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders scheduled
Oracle shares fell roughly 5.5% after the company filed SEC registration plans to issue $20 billion in new securities ($10B common stock, $10B senior notes) to help fund its AI data-center expansion
catalysts.note: Exact filing/announcement date not fully pinned down; grouped with the most recent dated trading data (Nov 6) found referencing it. Multiple RTTNews/StockStory items referencing large single-day moves (+7.8%, -7%) could not be reliably dated and were excluded.

catalysts.headline: Broader market and chip/tech stocks rebounded from the prior day's AI selloff (S&P 500 roughly +0.6% to ~7,395; Nasdaq Composite roughly +1.3% to ~24,626 late-day). Oracle traded higher intraday (roughly $116-$117, up ~1%-2% from the $115.16 Nov 5 close) but no confirmed Oracle-specific closing price was found this session.

Oracle's intraday decline was confirmed as a full-session close: ORCL finished 2026-11-05 at $115.16, down 6.93% from a $123.73 prior close, as part of a broad, market-wide AI-infrastructure selloff -- the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% (to 24,315.00) and the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (to 7,353.73), erasing roughly $3 trillion in market value. Coverage attributes the rout to post-midterm-election concern that political opposition could slow AI data-center buildout, compounded by a strong October jobs report reviving Fed rate-path concerns.

ORCL fell sharply intraday (roughly -7% to -8%, trading in the $114-115 area vs. a prior close of ~$123.77) amid a broad AI-infrastructure stock selloff following the U.S. midterm elections, on investor concern that political opposition to data-center development could slow AI buildouts; session range $111.66-$124.24, with $111.66 also the 52-week low.
catalysts.impact: -6.9% to -7.6% intraday depending on quote timestamp (not a confirmed close)

catalysts.headline: A Fool.com headline ('Stock Market Today, Nov. 4: Oracle Falls on Canceled $7 Billion Tencent Chip-Leasing Deal') attributes a same-day Oracle decline to cancellation of a reported $7B Tencent AI-chip leasing deal. This could not be corroborated: every other source located (Goldesel, TIKR, Boerse-Global, TrendForce, w.media, aiweekly.co) describes the Tencent deal only as FT-reported/signed around 2026-10-01 and still unconfirmed by either company, with no cancellation reported anywhere else found. See conflicts.
catalysts.impact: Cited as contributing to a two-day decline into 2026-11-05

catalysts.headline: Oracle held its Investor Day at AI World (Las Vegas): set an FY2030 revenue target of $225B+, a target of positive free cash flow in 2H FY2028, an FY2029 target of $30B+, and capped planned new capital-markets funding at $20B
catalysts.impact: Stock +10.73% on the session, closing $144.54 (from a prior close of ~$130.53)

catalysts.headline: Coverage of Oracle's AI-datacenter financing needs: company said it expects to raise roughly $40 billion in debt and equity in fiscal 2027 (having already raised $43B debt + $5B equity in FY2026); FY2026 capex rose to $55.7B from $21.2B in FY2025, and FY2027 capex guidance is $90-95B; FY2026 free cash flow was reported as negative $23.7B
catalysts.note: Secondary reporting on Oracle's FY2026 10-K disclosures; not independently fetched from the primary filing this session (SEC EDGAR unreachable).

catalysts.headline: Upcoming ex-dividend date for Oracle's regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.50/share (payable 2026-10-23); routine, part of the dividend program already in place, not a new declaration

Oracle fell ~4.7%-4.85% amid a broad AI-linked stock selloff, triggered by weekend comments from Anthropic and OpenAI leadership (including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, in a 2026-09-11 Fortune interview) urging a slower pace of frontier AI development and confirming OpenAI's IPO will not occur in 2026 (pushed to 2027 or later); compounded by ongoing concern over Oracle's debt-funded AI capex buildout (Q1 FY2027 capex $28.5B vs $8.5B a year earlier; FY2027 capex guidance maintained at $90B-$95B)
catalysts.impact: -4.7% to -4.85% on the day per multiple outlets

catalysts.headline: Oracle publicly rejected a Bloomberg report claiming certain OpenAI-committed data centers would slip to 2028 (a one-year delay from original schedule), stating 'There have been no delays on the sites required to meet our contractual commitments' and that timelines were jointly validated with OpenAI

Executive Chair/CTO Larry Ellison cancelled his Rule 10b5-1 trading plan (adopted 2026-06-22) that would have allowed sale of up to 50 million Oracle shares (~$7.5B); no shares were sold under the plan prior to cancellation; company gave no explanation, and Ellison stated he has no other plans to sell Oracle stock
catalysts.impact: cited by multiple outlets as a contributing factor in 2026-09-14 trading alongside the broader AI-sector selloff

catalysts.headline: Oracle disclosed (in a regulatory filing following its Q1 FY2027 close) that it is expanding its 2026 Restructuring Plan by approximately $700M, raising total estimated plan costs to roughly $2.8B (severance, contract termination, and related exit costs tied in part to AI-driven workforce reductions); ~$2.1B in charges had been recorded against the plan through 2026-08-31
catalysts.impact: cited as a contributing factor in the stock's decline

catalysts.headline: Oracle announced Q1 FY2027 results, driven by triple-digit growth in cloud infrastructure (OCI) revenue

FY2026 remaining performance obligations (RPO) reached $638B; disclosed $248B in additional off-balance-sheet lease commitments (15-19 year terms, 'substantially all related to data centers and cloud capacity'); disclosed $75B of customer-prepaid/supplied hardware reducing Oracle's own GPU capex burden
catalysts.note: Secondary reporting on the FY2026 10-K; exact filing date not pinned down (annual report would have been filed mid-2026) and not independently fetched this session.
